proposed.explanation:
Profit attributable to Talaat Moustafa Group's own shareholders (the parent-company line) rose from 9,025,066,065 EGP in 2024 (restated) to 14,383,890,306 EGP in 2025, an increase of 5,358,824,241 EGP or roughly 59.4 %. Consolidated net profit grew a similar 42.5 % (12,769,517,325 → 18,201,981,482 EGP), and EPS jumped from 4.38 to 6.98 EGP (+59.4 %). Total equity expanded from 129.9 bn to 157.7 bn EGP. These are strong one-year figures and support keeping the existing 500-share position for a 5-10-year growth horizon.

However, adding to the position is not possible under the diversification rule. Your current portfolio is 30,000 EGP cash + 500 × 82.50 = 41,250 EGP in TMGH, totalling 71,250 EGP. TMGH already represents 57.9 % of that total—above the 50 % cap. Buying even one more share would push the weight higher, so no purchase can satisfy the constraint. The only way to buy more TMGH would be to first sell other holdings (you have none) or to sell TMGH itself, which would be counter-productive.

Caveats: the evidence covers a single fiscal year (FY2025 vs. restated FY2024). There is no multi-year trend, no forward guidance, no valuation multiple (P/E, P/B), no dividend data, and no sector or macro context. One year of ~59 % profit growth is encouraging but does not by itself confirm a sustained 5-10-year growth trajectory. The restated 2024 figures also mean the prior-year base was adjusted, so part of the apparent growth may reflect accounting reclassification rather than purely operational improvement. Given your medium financial ability to withstand losses, maintaining the current position while monitoring future results is the prudent course. Revisit the decision when you have at least two more years of results and can assess whether the growth is durable.
